accuracy.evidence: Root meanings checked against Merriam-Webster and the Online Etymology Dictionary: tele- (Greek tēle, far), -scope (Greek skopein, to look at), micro- (Greek mikros, small), phon/phone (Greek phōnē, sound), bio- (Greek bios, life), -logy (Greek -logia, study of), graph (Greek graphein, write), auto- (self), aud (Latin audire, hear), vis (Latin videre/visus, see), port (Latin portare, carry), spect (Latin specere, look), dict (Latin dicere, say), rupt (Latin rumpere, break), sub (under), inter (between), trans (across), terra (earth), aqua (water), -ible/-able (able to be). 'expect' was confirmed as Latin exspectare (spect, look out for), which makes it a fair wrong option for the port question. 'phony' was confirmed as not from Greek phōnē (probably from 'fawney', a fake gilt ring), so it is a true false friend. Standards: CCSS L.4.4b/L.5.4b; NC England Years 5-6 reading word reading (morphology and etymology).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors reported in morphology teaching (Bowers & Kirby 2010; EEF Improving Literacy in KS2 on morphology): splitting at a letter string rather than a meaning unit (step 1 wrong gaps: 'tel + escope: those are not parts with a meaning'), confusing look-alike morphemes bi/bio (step 2 prediction, tag bi, p2) and -logy/graph (tag logy), choosing a prefix with the wrong meaning (sub/inter for trans), trusting a look-alike root over context (phony, step 4 prediction, tag false, m6), and reversing the order when building (step 5 'Right parts, wrong order').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagroot is built on morpheme mechanics: tapping the join between letters to split a word, assigning a meaning to each part to assemble a definition, sorting by Latin root family, decoding in a sentence with a false-friend check, and building a word from two meaning tiles in order. flagwfam (843, native word families like act/action), flagorigin (797, spelling patterns of Greek/French/Latin words) and flagpfx (853, prefix meanings and spelling joins) teach different things; the gate measured under 30% shingle overlap.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner works out the routine before the text names it: the split shows each part with its meaning, the meaning step fills in each part's meaning card and then prints the combined definition, the sort shows families collecting under their root, and the phony item makes the learner see the sentence overrule the root. The closing text 'Roots are strong clues, but the sentence has the last word' confirms what was just found.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: tele = 'screen' (from television), bio = 'two' (bi- in bicycle), and phony = 'about sound' because it looks like phon. Each is then disproved in the lab (telephone and telescope have no screen; bi vs bio feedback; the sentence about painted metal).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, two wrong options each with a specific message: 'under is sub-, as in submarine. trans- means across', 'bi- means two, but bio means life', '-logy is study of. graph means write', 'expect comes from spect, look', 'phony only looks like phon...', 'One letter tells you nothing'. In-lab wrong taps name the part and its real meaning ('aud means hear, as in audio and audience. vis means see.').

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes; kid paragraphs grade 2.8, adult 8.6. Canvas text is one heading plus a short sub-line per state; meaning cards are one or two words.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Every step has one job (split, meaning, family, decode with context, build) and every feedback line names a root and its meaning.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for every step before and after Show me: nine letter tiles of 'microphone' fit the width, the three family boxes and the 3 x 3 tile grid fit without clipping, and option text wraps inside its box. After the first screenshots showed the 14 px gap targets were small, the canvas tap now picks the nearest gap anywhere along the letter row, and every gap also has a full-size button below.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a Lab button with an aria-label (e.g. 'Split after tele', 'micro means small', 'Put in the spect: look family', 'tele, means far'); the canvas aria-label and c.say live text read the word, the current question and what has been picked. Walkthrough and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) pass in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
